_purpose: Non-contractual delivery parameters the schedule and queue compute against.
_why_separate: None of this is in the signed agreement. Capacity is what the consultant can commit; the agreement fixes dates and hours. Keeping them apart stops a capacity assumption being read as a contractual term.
capacity_source: D-6, docs/Import/baseline-lock.yml — 'I can commit 16 hours a week physically, but use AI to deploy so move much more work.'
estimating_rule_meaning: Estimates stay at the WBS figures. Do not re-estimate downward because AI assistance is expected — the WBS is the accepted specification (D-5).
Schedule risk is computed against physical capacity, not against expected AI throughput.
Actual hours are expected well below estimate. A large negative Delta is the expected outcome, not a signal that the estimate was wrong.
Nothing may ever propose an actual AT the estimate value (IMP-0032).

testing_and_acceptance.live_operational_use: NONE — everything is in development (reviewer, 2026-08-19). Build Terms B5 route 3 has not fired for any deliverable.

client_testing.scope: Phase 2 as built so far — columns, views and form layout
client_testing.why_not: Handing work over to be tested is not submitting the phase for acceptance. If it were, B5's ten-business-day clock would start and silence during testing would accept the phase by default. Recorded as a V4 review, not a submission.
client_testing.verification_level: V4 — a named person opens the components and looks at them

client_acceptance.when: after the Client has tested in the acceptance environment
client_acceptance.blocked_on: promotion DEV -> TST/ACC, which is a manual step in the Power Platform Pipelines UI (ADR-007). Nothing has been promoted beyond DEV.
client_acceptance.environment: tst_acc — Test and Acceptance are one environment (TAD ADR-006)
